# Project file

<!-- Generated by `chipload reference`; do not edit. Regenerate with CHIPLOAD_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p chipload-cli --test guide. -->

A project (`.chipload`) is a JSON file. Chipload writes every field; when you write one by hand or with a script, the fields marked *no* may be left out. Lengths are in mm, angles in radians, feeds in mm/min. `chipload schema project` prints the JSON Schema this page is made from.

Schema version 33. Older files load through Chipload's migrations; this schema describes only the current version.

## The file

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `active_part` | integer or null | no | The part new operations go into (its id). Null or no such part: the first part. Only the app and the command line read it; it changes nothing that is cut. |
| `drawing` | [Drawing](#drawing) | yes | The drawing: the shapes Chipload cuts, imported from a DXF or drawn in Chipload. |
| `machine` | [Machine](#machine) | yes | The machine: post-processor, safe height, limits and zero. |
| `operations` | list of [Operation](#operation) | yes | The operations, cut in this order: grouped by part, in the parts' order. |
| `parts` | list of [Part](#part) | yes | The parts: groups of operations, each cut with its copies before the next part. At least one. |
| `schema_version` | `33` | yes | The version of the file format. Chipload upgrades older files when it reads them, and refuses newer ones. |
| `stock` | [Stock](#stock) | yes | The material on the machine. |
| `tools` | list of [Tool](#tool) | yes | The tools the operations cut with. |
| `written_by` | string or null | no | The Chipload version that wrote the file, for reference. |

## ArcSegment

From `start_angle` through `sweep` radians (positive = counter-clockwise).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `center` | 2 × number | yes | Centre, mm. |
| `radius` | number | yes | Radius, mm. |
| `start_angle` | number | yes | Where the arc starts, radians from +X, counter-clockwise. |
| `sweep` | number | yes | How far it turns, radians: positive counter-clockwise. |

## AutoThreshold

The word "auto".

One of: `"auto"`.

## Bone

What a chosen corner gets.

One of: `"none"`, `"dogbone"`, `"tbone"`.

## Copies

A grid of copies of a part: copy (column c, row r) is the part moved by (c·dx, r·dy) mm.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `columns` | integer | yes | Copies along X, at least 1. |
| `dx` | number | yes | Distance from copy to copy along X, mm; negative grows to the left. |
| `dy` | number | yes | Distance from copy to copy along Y, mm; negative grows downwards. |
| `order` | [CopyOrder](#copyorder) | no | `by_operation`: each operation on every copy, then the next; `by_copy`: every operation on one copy, then the next copy. |
| `rows` | integer | yes | Copies along Y, at least 1. |

## CopyOrder

In which order the copies are cut.

- `"by_operation"`: Each operation on every copy, then the next operation.

- `"by_copy"`: Every operation on one copy, then the next copy. Called `by_part` before parts came (schema 22).

## CornerChoice

A corner with its own bone, chosen by the user.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `along` | [Wall](#wall) or null | no | The wall a T-bone runs along, `longer` or `shorter`: the notch is in the other. Required with a T-bone; null otherwise. |
| `at` | 2 × number | yes | The corner, in drawing coordinates (mm). |
| `bone` | [Bone](#bone) | yes | `none` (the corner stays round), `dogbone` or `tbone`. |

## Corners

How the tool reaches into the inside corners it would leave round, so a square part fits: every corner on the tool's side up to `max_angle`.

### `"type": "dogbone"`

In along the corner's bisector.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_angle` | number | yes | Only corners this sharp or sharper, radians (1.745 = 100°). |

### `"type": "tbone"`

In along the longer wall: the notch is in the shorter one.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_angle` | number | yes | Only corners this sharp or sharper, radians (1.745 = 100°). |

## CustomPost

A user post-processor's config and template, exactly as read from the posts folder.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config` | string | yes | The post's settings file (TOML), as copied. |
| `template` | string | yes | The post's template, as copied. |

## Direction

One of: `"climb"`, `"conventional"`.

## Drawing

The project's drawing: shapes in millimetres, or (only for jobs from before v4) a reference to a DXF that still has to be embedded.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dxfs` | list of [DrawingSource](#drawingsource) | no | The DXFs the imported shapes came from, each as at its last import or update, with its own placement. |
| `hidden` | list of string | no | Groups and layers not drawn on the canvas (they are still cut): `dxf:1`, `dxf:1/layer:Cut`, `image:1`, `text:1`, `drawn:circle`, `drawn:rectangle`, `drawn:polyline`. |
| `images` | list of [Image](#image) | no | Pictures traced into shapes, for V-carving. |
| `next_shape_id` | integer | yes | The id the next new shape gets. Ids are never reused. |
| `shapes` | list of [Shape](#shape) | yes | The shapes, imported and drawn. |
| `texts` | list of [Text](#text) | no | Texts written into shapes, for V-carving, pocketing or profiling. Left out of the file when there are none, so projects without text open in older versions. |

## DrawingFormat

A drawing file's format.

One of: `"dxf"`, `"svg"`.

## DrawingSource

Provenance of the imported shapes.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | string | yes | The DXF's file name. |
| `flattened` | object | no | How many curves of each type (splines, ellipses) were turned into arcs. |
| `format` | [DrawingFormat](#drawingformat) | yes | What kind of file it is: a DXF or an SVG. |
| `id` | integer | yes | The DXF's id, which its shapes and selectors name. |
| `ignored` | object | no | How many entities of each type were left out (text, dimensions, …). |
| `imported` | object | no | How many entities of each type were imported. |
| `issues` | list of [SourceIssue](#sourceissue) | no | What the import found: the import report. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its name in the Browser and messages; the file's name without its extension at first. |
| `placement` | [Placement](#placement) | yes | How the imported drawing was moved, turned and scaled on the stock. |
| `px_per_inch` | number or null | no | An SVG without a real size: the pixels per inch chosen for it, used again on update. None for a DXF and an SVG with real units. |
| `sha256` | string | yes | The DXF's SHA-256, to tell whether it changed. |
| `units` | [Units](#units) | yes | The DXF's units: `mm` or `inch`. Inch drawings are converted to mm on import. |
| `units_from` | [UnitsFrom](#unitsfrom) | yes | Where the units came from: the DXF itself, or the user's choice. |

## Entry

How the tool goes down into the material at the start of each pass, for pockets and follow paths (a profile always spirals: its `ramp_angle`).

### `"type": "plunge"`

Straight down: needs a centre-cutting tool. An empty struct variant, as `Rings`.

### `"type": "ramp"`

Down along the path and back, never steeper than `ramp_angle` (radians, 0 < angle <= 30°).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ramp_angle` | number | yes | The steepest the ramp goes, radians: more than 0, at most 30° (0.5236). |

### `"type": "helix"`

Pockets only: down round a circle of `radius` (the tool centre's), never steeper than `ramp_angle`.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | number | yes | The helix's radius, mm: less than the tool radius. |
| `ramp_angle` | number | yes | The steepest the helix goes, radians: more than 0, at most 30° (0.5236). |

## Finish

A finishing pass on a profile.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stock` | number | yes | Left on the wall by the roughing passes, mm: more than 0, less than the tool radius. |

## HoleMethod

How a Holes operation cuts.

### `"type": "drill"`

Straight down at the hole's centre, `peck` mm at a time.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `peck` | number or null | no | Drill this many mm at a time, lifting out between pecks to clear chips. Null: in one go. |

### `"type": "bore"`

A helix at the wall, at most `step_down` mm per turn and never steeper than `ramp_angle` (radians, 0 < angle <= 30°), then one level circle.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `direction` | [Direction](#direction) | yes | `climb` or `conventional`, as for a profile inside the hole. |
| `ramp_angle` | number | yes | The steepest the helix goes, radians: more than 0, at most 30° (0.5236). |
| `step_down` | number | yes | The most the helix goes down per turn, mm. |

## Image

A picture traced into shapes: the picture itself, where it goes, and how it becomes black and white. Its traced shapes are `path` shapes on its layer that name it in `image`.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `arcs` | boolean | yes | Traced edges are fitted with arcs as well as lines. |
| `blur` | number | yes | Blur before the threshold, in pixels, 0 to 10; 0: none. |
| `data` | string | yes | The picture file itself (PNG, JPEG or BMP), base64-encoded. |
| `file` | string | yes | The picture's file name. |
| `id` | integer | yes | The image's id, which its traced shapes name. |
| `invert` | boolean | yes | Carve the light parts instead of the dark ones. |
| `layer` | string | yes | The layer its traced shapes go on. |
| `min_area` | number | yes | Black or white specks smaller than this are dropped, mm², 0 to 100. |
| `rotation` | number | yes | Turned counter-clockwise about the picture's centre, degrees, at least 0 and less than 360. `x`, `y` and `width` are before the turn; the traced shapes are turned after the trace. |
| `sha256` | string | yes | The picture's SHA-256. |
| `smoothing` | number | yes | How far a traced edge may be simplified away from the picture's edge, mm, 0.01 to 1. |
| `threshold` | [ImageThreshold](#imagethreshold) | yes | Grey values below this (0–255) are black: 1 to 254, or "auto" to pick it from the picture (Otsu's method). |
| `trace` | [ImageTrace](#imagetrace) | yes | What it is traced into: the black parts' outlines (for a V-carve) or their centre lines (for a follow path). |
| `width` | number | yes | The picture's width on the stock, mm; its height follows from the picture. |
| `x` | number | yes | X of the picture's lower-left corner on the stock, mm. |
| `y` | number | yes | Y of the picture's lower-left corner on the stock, mm. |

## ImageThreshold

Where grey turns black: "auto" or a grey value.

- [AutoThreshold](#autothreshold): Picked from the picture.

- integer: Grey values below this are black, 1 to 254.

## ImageTrace

What a picture is traced into.

- `"outline"`: Closed outlines round the black parts, black inside.

- `"centre_line"`: Open (or closed) paths along the black strokes' middles.

## IssueSeverity

One of: `"warning"`, `"error"`.

## Lead

Quarter-circle lead-in and lead-out.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | number | yes | Radius of the lead arcs, mm: more than 0, at most 10 tool diameters. Smaller where there's no room. |

## LineSegment

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `end` | 2 × number | yes | End point, mm. |
| `start` | 2 × number | yes | Start point, mm. |

## Machine

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `custom_post` | [CustomPost](#custompost) or null | no | Your own post-processor, copied into the project when chosen, so it gives the same G-code anywhere. Null: `post` is a built-in one. |
| `gcode_units` | [Units](#units) | yes | The units the G-code is written in: `mm` (G21) or `inch` (G20). Everything else in the project stays in mm. Since schema 28. |
| `library_uid` | string or null | no | The `uid` of the machine profile these values came from, for reference; nothing that cuts reads it. Null: not from a profile. |
| `max_feed` | number or null | no | The machine's fastest feed, mm/min: higher feeds are refused, and the cycle time uses it for rapids. Null: unknown. |
| `name` | string or null | no | The machine profile these values came from, for reference; nothing reads it. |
| `post` | string | yes | The post-processor: `grbl`, `linuxcnc`, `mach3`, or the name of your own. |
| `safe_z` | number | yes | The height for rapid moves sideways, mm above Z0. Above the stock top. |
| `spindle` | [Spindle](#spindle) | yes | The spindle's direction: `cw` (M3) or `ccw` (M4). |
| `tool_change` | [ToolChange](#toolchange) | yes | With several tools: `files` (one file per tool) or `program` (one file with tool changes). |
| `travel` | [Travel](#travel) or null | no | The machine's travel, mm. When set, a program that moves farther is refused. Null: not checked. |
| `work_zero` | [WorkZero](#workzero) | no | The point of the drawing that becomes X0 Y0 in the G-code. Missing: the drawing's origin. |

## MaterialRef

A library material, as a project names it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `library_uid` | string | yes | The library material's uid. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its name when chosen, shown when the library no longer has it. |

## Operation

### `"type": "profile"`

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clearance` | number | yes | How far the cut moves into the material that is kept, mm: positive removes more (a larger pocket, a smaller part), negative leaves material. Less than the tool radius. |
| `corner_choices` | list of [CornerChoice](#cornerchoice) | no | Corners with their own bone, whatever `corners` says. Missing or empty: none. Left out when empty. |
| `corners` | [Corners](#corners) or null | no | Dogbones or T-bones in the inside corners, so square parts fit. Null: the corners stay round. |
| `direction` | [Direction](#direction) | yes | `climb` or `conventional` milling. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | False: the operation stays in the project but isn't cut. Missing: true. |
| `end_depth` | number | yes | Where the cut ends, mm down from the stock top. More than the start depth; below the stock bottom only within `stock.max_overcut`. |
| `feed` | number | yes | The cutting feed, mm/min. |
| `finish` | [Finish](#finish) or null | no | A finishing pass: the roughing passes leave `stock` mm on the wall, and one last lap at full depth takes it off. Null: none. |
| `material` | [MaterialRef](#materialref) or null | no | The library material its feeds come from. Null: its own values. |
| `name` | string | no | A name for the operation, shown in the list and on the setup sheet. Empty: none. |
| `part` | integer | yes | The id of the part it belongs to (`parts`). |
| `plunge_feed` | number | yes | The feed going down into the material, mm/min. |
| `ramp_angle` | number | yes | The steepest the spiral ramp goes down along the contour, radians: more than 0, at most 30° (0.5236). A profile always spirals down (docs/specs/profile-always-spiral.md). |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | yes | What the operation cuts: the shapes on a layer, or shapes by id. |
| `side` | [Side](#side) | yes | Which side of the line the tool cuts: `outside` (cutting a part out), `inside` (a hole) or `on` the line. |
| `skin` | [Skin](#skin) or null | no | An onion skin: the passes stop `thickness` mm above the end depth, and one last lap cuts through it. Null: none. |
| `start_depth` | number | yes | Where the cut starts, mm down from the stock top: 0 for the top, more when an earlier operation already cut down to there. |
| `starts` | list of 2 × number | no | Where the cut starts, as points in drawing coordinates (mm): each moves the start of the ring (contour) nearest to it. Empty: chosen by Chipload. |
| `step_down` | number | yes | The deepest each pass goes, mm. The passes are equal, and the last one ends exactly at the end depth. |
| `tabs` | [Tabs](#tabs) or null | no | Holding tabs left at the bottom of the cut, so a part cut out doesn't come loose. Null: none. |
| `tool` | integer | yes | The id of the project tool it cuts with (`tools`). |

### `"type": "pocket"`

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clearance` | number | yes | How far the cut moves into the material that is kept, mm: positive removes more (a larger pocket, a smaller part), negative leaves material. Less than the tool radius. |
| `corner_choices` | list of [CornerChoice](#cornerchoice) | no | Corners with their own bone, whatever `corners` says. Missing or empty: none. Left out when empty. |
| `corners` | [Corners](#corners) or null | no | Dogbones or T-bones in the inside corners, so square parts fit. Null: the corners stay round. |
| `direction` | [Direction](#direction) | yes | `climb` or `conventional` milling. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | False: the operation stays in the project but isn't cut. Missing: true. |
| `end_depth` | number | yes | Where the cut ends, mm down from the stock top. More than the start depth; below the stock bottom only within `stock.max_overcut`. |
| `entry` | [Entry](#entry) | no | How the tool goes down at the start of each pass: `plunge` (straight down; needs a centre-cutting tool) or `ramp` along the path; pockets also `helix`. Missing: plunge. |
| `feed` | number | yes | The cutting feed, mm/min. |
| `lead` | [Lead](#lead) or null | no | A quarter-circle lead-in and lead-out from the cleared side onto the wall. Null: none. |
| `material` | [MaterialRef](#materialref) or null | no | The library material its feeds come from. Null: its own values. |
| `name` | string | no | A name for the operation, shown in the list and on the setup sheet. Empty: none. |
| `part` | integer | yes | The id of the part it belongs to (`parts`). |
| `plunge_feed` | number | yes | The feed going down into the material, mm/min. |
| `rest` | [Rest](#rest) or null | no | Rest machining: clear only what a larger tool leaves in these shapes. Null: the whole pocket. |
| `rest_passes` | list of [RestPass](#restpass) | no | Rest passes: smaller endmills that clear what this pocket's tool (or the pass before) leaves, in its shapes and depths. Missing or empty: none. Left out when empty. |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | yes | What the operation cuts: the shapes on a layer, or shapes by id. |
| `start_depth` | number | yes | Where the cut starts, mm down from the stock top: 0 for the top, more when an earlier operation already cut down to there. |
| `starts` | list of 2 × number | no | Where each wall ring starts, as points in drawing coordinates (mm): each moves the start of the wall ring nearest to it. Empty: chosen by Chipload. |
| `step_down` | number | yes | The deepest each pass goes, mm. The passes are equal, and the last one ends exactly at the end depth. |
| `stepover` | number | yes | The distance between the clearing rings, as a fraction of the tool diameter: more than 0, at most 1. |
| `tool` | integer | yes | The id of the project tool it cuts with (`tools`). |

### `"type": "vcarve"`

V-carve: a V-bit follows the centre line of closed shapes, as deep as makes the cut exactly as wide as the shape.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | no | False: the operation stays in the project but isn't cut. Missing: true. |
| `end_depth` | number | yes | The deepest the V-bit's tip may go, mm down from the stock top. Strokes that need more are carved to it, narrower than drawn, with a warning. |
| `feed` | number | yes | The feed, mm/min, for moves no steeper than 45°. |
| `material` | [MaterialRef](#materialref) or null | no | The library material its feeds come from. Null: its own values. |
| `name` | string | no | A name for the operation, shown in the list and on the setup sheet. Empty: none. |
| `part` | integer | yes | The id of the part it belongs to (`parts`). |
| `plunge_feed` | number | yes | The feed for moves steeper than 45°, mm/min. |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | yes | What the operation cuts: the shapes on a layer, or shapes by id. |
| `start_depth` | number | yes | The surface carved, mm down from the stock top: 0 for the top, more to carve on a floor an earlier pocket cut. |
| `step_down` | number or null | no | Carve in passes no deeper than this, mm. Null: one pass. |
| `tool` | integer | yes | The id of the project tool it cuts with (`tools`). |

| `part` | integer | yes | The id of the part it belongs to (`parts`). |
| `plunge_feed` | number | yes | The feed going down into the material, mm/min. |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | yes | What the operation cuts: the shapes on a layer, or shapes by id. |
| `start_depth` | number | yes | Where the cut starts, mm down from the stock top: 0 for the top, more when an earlier operation already cut down to there. |

### `"type": "holes"`

Holes: drilled with a drill, bored with a helix with an endmill.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | no | False: the operation stays in the project but isn't cut. Missing: true. |
| `end_depth` | number | yes | Where the hole ends, mm down from the stock top. For a drill, the depth of its point. |

| `plunge_feed` | number | yes | A drill's feed down, or a bore's feed straight down to the start depth, mm/min. |

| `start_depth` | number | yes | Where the cut starts, mm down from the stock top: 0 for the top, more when an earlier operation already cut down to there. |
| `tool` | integer | yes | The id of the project tool it cuts with (`tools`). |

### `"type": "surface"`

Surface: the whole stock top taken down flat, in straight passes back and forth.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | no | False: the operation stays in the project but isn't cut. Missing: true. |
| `end_depth` | number | yes | How far down the stock top is taken, mm. At most the stock thickness. |
| `feed` | number | yes | The cutting feed, mm/min. |

| `name` | string | no | A name for the operation, shown in the list and on the setup sheet. Empty: none. |
| `part` | integer | yes | The id of the part it belongs to (`parts`). The stock is faced once, whatever copies the part has. |

| `start_depth` | number | yes | Where the cut starts, mm down from the stock top: 0 for the top. |
| `step_down` | number | yes | The deepest each pass goes, mm. The passes are equal, and the last one ends exactly at the end depth. |
| `stepover` | number | yes | The distance between passes, as a fraction of the tool diameter: at least 0.1, at most 0.9. |
| `tool` | integer | yes | The id of the project tool it cuts with (`tools`): an endmill. |

## Part

A part: a named group of operations, cut together, with its own copies (docs/specs/parts.md §2). It owns no geometry: its operations select the shapes.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `copies` | [Copies](#copies) or null | no | Cut the part several times in a grid. Null: once. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | False: the part and all its operations stay in the project but aren't cut. |
| `id` | integer | yes | Its number, unique in the project: what operations name it by. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its name, unique in the project, shown in the Browser, the report and the sheet. |

## Placement

Where the imported drawing is put: a DXF point p goes to scale · rotate(p) + (dx, dy), turned and scaled about the DXF's origin.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dx` | number | yes | Then moved along X, mm. |
| `dy` | number | yes | Then moved along Y, mm. |
| `rotation` | number | yes | Turned counter-clockwise about the DXF's origin, degrees, at least 0 and less than 360, after the scale. Multiples of 90 are exact. |
| `scale` | number | yes | Scaled about the DXF's origin by this factor, 0.001 to 1000; 1: as drawn. |

## Rest

Rest machining: the pocket clears only the material the larger tool `after_tool` can't reach in its shapes.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `after_tool` | integer | yes | The id of the larger project tool whose leftovers this pocket clears. |

## RestPass

One rest pass of a pocket (docs/specs/rest-passes.md §2): it takes the pocket's shapes, depths, clearance and direction, and clears only what the tool before it leaves.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | no | False: kept, but not cut. Missing: true. |
| `entry` | [Entry](#entry) | yes | How the tool goes down: `plunge`, `ramp` or `helix`. |
| `feed` | number | yes | The cutting feed, mm/min. |
| `plunge_feed` | number | yes | The feed going down into the material, mm/min. |
| `step_down` | number | yes | The deepest each pass goes, mm. |
| `stepover` | number | yes | The distance between the clearing rings, as a fraction of the tool diameter. |
| `tool` | integer | yes | The id of the project tool it cuts with (`tools`): an endmill smaller than the tool before it. |

## Selector

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dxf` | integer or null | no | Only shapes from this DXF (an id in `drawing.dxfs`). |
| `exclude` | list of integer or null | no | Shapes of that DXF, image or text left out (ids); with `dxf`, `image` or `text` only. A contour with any of them isn't cut. A traced image's, or a text's, are found again when it is made again. |
| `image` | integer or null | no | Only shapes traced from this image (an id in `drawing.images`). |
| `layer` | string or null | no | Every shape on this layer (upper or lower case don't matter). |
| `shapes` | list of integer or null | no | These shapes, by id. |
| `text` | integer or null | no | Only the letters of this text (an id in `drawing.texts`). |

## Shape

One shape of the drawing: imported from a DXF (`path`: lines and arcs, one shape per DXF entity), or drawn in Chipload (`circle`, `rectangle`, `polyline`). One flat object: `id`, `layer`, `kind`, then the fields of that kind.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `angle` | number or null | no | rectangle: its rotation about the centre; polygon: the angle of its first corner from +X; radians, counter-clockwise. |
| `bulges` | list of number or null | no | polyline: one per segment, as in DXF: tan(sweep / 4); 0 straight, 1 a counter-clockwise half circle, -1 clockwise. |
| `center` | 2 × number or null | no | circle, rectangle, polygon: the centre, mm. |
| `closed` | boolean or null | no | path, polyline: whether it ends where it starts. |
| `construction` | boolean | no | circle, rectangle, polygon, polyline: construction geometry, shown and snapped to but never cut; left out when false. |
| `corner_radius` | number or null | no | rectangle: the radius of its corners, mm; 0 for sharp ones. |
| `dxf` | integer or null | no | path: the DXF it was imported from (its id in `drawing.dxfs`). |
| `dxf_handle` | string or null | no | path: the handle of the DXF entity it came from, which keeps its id when the DXF is updated. |
| `dxf_type` | string or null | no | path: the DXF entity's type, e.g. LWPOLYLINE. |
| `id` | integer | yes | The shape's id, which operations select it by. |
| `image` | integer or null | no | path: the image it was traced from; absent for shapes from a DXF. |
| `kind` | [ShapeKind](#shapekind) | yes | `path` (imported from a DXF), or a shape drawn in Chipload: `circle`, `rectangle`, `polyline`. |
| `layer` | string | yes | Its layer. |
| `length` | number or null | no | rectangle: its size along its own X axis, mm. |
| `name` | string or null | no | circle, rectangle, polyline: its name in the Browser; left out when it has none. |
| `points` | list of 2 × number or null | no | polyline: its points, mm. |
| `radius` | number or null | no | circle: the radius, mm; polygon: the radius to its corners, mm. |
| `segments` | list of [PathSegment](#pathsegment) or null | no | path: its lines and arcs, mm. |
| `sides` | integer or null | no | polygon: how many sides (and corners) it has, 3 to 1000. |
| `text` | integer or null | no | path: the text it is a letter of (its id in `drawing.texts`). |
| `width` | number or null | no | rectangle: its size along its own Y axis, mm. |

## ShapeKind

One of: `"path"`, `"circle"`, `"rectangle"`, `"polyline"`, `"polygon"`.

## Side

One of: `"inside"`, `"outside"`, `"on"`.

## Skin

An onion skin on a profile.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `thickness` | number | yes | Left above the end depth until the last lap, mm: more than 0, at most the step down. |

## SourceIssue

An import-time issue that can't be recomputed from the shapes.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | yes | What kind of issue, e.g. `duplicate` or `open_contour` (see the import page of the guide). |
| `message` | string | yes | What it is, in words. |
| `severity` | [IssueSeverity](#issueseverity) | yes | `warning` or `error`. |

## Spindle

- `"cw"`: M3

- `"ccw"`: M4

## Stock

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fit` | number or null | no | Centred on the drawing only: its size is the drawing's outline plus this margin each side, mm, following the drawing; `x` and `y` are then used only while the drawing is empty. Null: the size is `x` × `y`. |
| `material` | [MaterialRef](#materialref) or null | no | The project's material: new operations take it, with its values. Each operation names its own (`material` on the operation). Null: none. |
| `max_overcut` | number | yes | How far a cut may go below the stock bottom, into the spoilboard, mm. |
| `origin` | [StockOrigin](#stockorigin) | no | Where the stock lies: its `bottom_left` corner or its `center` at the drawing's origin, or centred on the drawing itself (`drawing`), following it. |
| `thickness` | number | yes | Thickness, mm. Depths count down from the top. |
| `x` | number | yes | Size along X, mm. |
| `y` | number | yes | Size along Y, mm. |
| `z_zero` | [ZZero](#zzero) | no | Where Z0 is: the stock `top` or `bottom`. |

## StockCorner

One of: `"center"`, `"bottom_left"`, `"bottom_right"`, `"top_left"`, `"top_right"`.

## StockOrigin

- `"bottom_left"`, `"center"`: 

- `"drawing"`: Centred on the drawing's outline, sticking out equally all round, and following the drawing when it moves or changes (the user, 2026-10-28). Construction geometry doesn't count; an empty drawing centres it on the origin.

## Tabs

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | list of 2 × number | no | Tab centres placed by hand, in drawing coordinates (mm): a contour with points gets exactly those tabs, one without gets `count`, evenly spaced. Left out when empty. |
| `count` | integer | yes | Tabs per contour, at least 1. |
| `flank_angle` | number | yes | The slope of the tab's sides, radians: π/2 (90°) straight, less for sloped tabs a ramped profile follows. |
| `height` | number | yes | The bridge's thickness, up from the bottom of the cut, mm. |
| `width` | number | yes | The bridge left on the part, along its edge, mm (the flat top of a sloped tab). |

## Text

A text written into shapes: what it says, its font and size, and where it goes. Its letters are `path` shapes on its layer that name it in `text`, made again when it changes; the font is needed only for that, not to cut them.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `align` | [TextAlign](#textalign) | yes | How the lines line up against each other. |
| `anchor` | [TextAnchor](#textanchor) | no | What `x` and `y` are: the box's lower-left corner (before the turn), or its centre. A centred text stays centred there when its words, font or size change. Missing: the corner. |
| `font` | string | yes | A built-in font: FreeSans, FreeSans Bold, FreeSerif, FreeSerif Bold, FreeMono or FreeMono Bold (`chipload text fonts`). |
| `height` | number | yes | The height of a capital letter, mm. |
| `id` | integer | yes | The text's id, which its letters name. |
| `layer` | string | yes | The layer its letters go on. |
| `line_spacing` | number | yes | From one line's base to the next, in capital heights. |
| `rotation` | number | yes | Turned counter-clockwise about the box's centre, degrees, at least 0 and less than 360. |
| `spacing` | number | yes | Extra space between letters, mm; 0: the font's own spacing, kerning included. |
| `text` | string | yes | What it says; a line break ("\n") starts a new line. |
| `x` | number | yes | X of the text's anchor on the stock, mm: the lower-left corner of its box (before the turn) or its centre. |
| `y` | number | yes | Y of the text's anchor on the stock, mm. |

## TextAlign

How a text's lines line up.

One of: `"left"`, `"center"`, `"right"`.

## TextAnchor

What a text's position is (docs/specs/text.md §3).

- `"corner"`: The lower-left corner of the text's box, before the turn.

- `"center"`: The centre of the text's box (the turn keeps it in place).

## Tool

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `angle` | number or null | no | V-bits: the included angle, radians. Null: unknown; a V-carve then refuses the tool. |
| `center_cutting` | boolean or null | no | Whether it can plunge straight down. False: profiles ramp in and pockets go down round a helix. Null: unknown. |
| `diameter` | number | yes | Diameter, mm. For a V-bit, its widest cutting diameter. |
| `flutes` | integer or null | no | Number of flutes, for the chip load. Null: unknown. |
| `id` | integer | yes | The tool's number: what operations name it by, and its T number in the G-code. |
| `library_uid` | string or null | no | The `uid` of the library tool it came from, for reference; nothing that cuts reads it. Null: not from the library. |
| `name` | string or null | no | The library tool it came from, for reference. |
| `rpm` | number or null | no | Spindle speed, rpm. Needed to generate. |
| `tip_diameter` | number or null | no | V-bits: the flat tip's diameter, mm. Null: pointed. |
| `type` | [ToolType](#tooltype) | no | `endmill`, `drill` or `vbit`. |

## ToolChange

How a job with several tools is written.

- `"files"`: One G-code file per tool group; the user changes the tool and sets Z zero between.

- `"program"`: One file with `T<n> M6` at each change, for a sender that handles it.

## ToolType

One of: `"endmill"`, `"drill"`, `"vbit"`.

## Travel

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | number | yes | Travel along X, mm. |
| `y` | number | yes | Travel along Y, mm. |
| `z` | number | yes | Travel along Z, mm. |

## Units

One of: `"mm"`, `"inch"`.

## UnitsFrom

- `"dxf"`: Declared by the file: a DXF's $INSUNITS, an SVG's size in real units.

- `"user"`: The file declared none; the user chose (a DXF's units, an SVG's pixels per inch).

## Wall

One of a corner's two walls, by length.

One of: `"longer"`, `"shorter"`.

## WorkZero

Where the G-code's X0 Y0 is. The geometry never moves; only the output is translated.

- object: The drawing's own origin (the only choice before work_zero existed). An empty struct variant, not a unit one, so serde refuses stray fields here too.

- object: A corner or the centre of the stock, as placed by `stock.origin`.

- object: Any point, in drawing coordinates (mm).

## ZZero

One of: `"top"`, `"bottom"`.
